entries.definition: A clustering algorithm that alternates nearest-feature-mean assignments and mean updates to minimize within-cluster squared distances in a kernel-defined feature space, with an observation-weighted extension.

paper_readings.version: Final IEEE TNN 20(7):1181-1194, July 2009; DOI 10.1109/TNN.2009.2019722. Printed page = PDF page + 1180. Source mentions a separate 2008 conference precursor, which has not been downloaded/read in this round.
paper_readings.abstract_interpretation: The authors address kernel k-means initialization through incremental deterministic cluster addition. Full global search over datum seeds has two named accelerations: a one-seed lower-bound criterion and CMM-selected candidate exemplars. Positive observation-weight extensions support graph objectives. Near-optimality and empirical superiority are author claims, not approximation certificates.

passages.locator: PDF pp. 2-3 / printed pp. 1182-1183, Section II-B, Algorithm 1, Equations 2-3
passages.reading: Kernel k-means represents each feature center as the mean of current assigned features, and assigns all points to nearest centers before recomputing the groups. Distances use Gram entries. For a fixed PSD Gram matrix this decreases the objective subject to well-defined nonempty clusters; sign/zero-distance ties and empty clusters need conventions. Feature means are explicit RKHS sums even when input preimages or coordinates are unavailable. Table I lists a sigmoid kernel without universal parameter validity; do not infer arbitrary tanh is PSD. Kernel-PCA equivalence needs all retained nonzero feature coordinates, not arbitrary truncation.

passages.locator: PDF pp. 3-4 / pp. 1183-1184, Section III-A, Algorithm 2
passages.reading: Start with the single cluster. At each k=2..M, try each datum x_n as a singleton new cluster and remove it from its previous cluster C_r; keep other groups. Run kernel k-means for each initialization and retain least objective solution. Source explicit disjoint partition differs from leaving old centers unchanged and simply adding a center. Empty singleton-source clusters are not resolved in pseudocode. Preserve as an implementation limitation or inspect released code. Determinism requires tie policies. The paper explicitly lacks a near-optimality theorem; no approximation ratio or guaranteed global optimum.

passages.locator: PDF p. 4 / p. 1184, Section IV-A, Equation 4
passages.reading: Fast global kernel k-means chooses n maximizing b_n=sum_i max(d_i_old - ||phi(x_n)-phi(x_i)||^2,0), then runs a single kernel k-means stage. The source calls E_old-b_n an upper bound on final error via allocation to old centers plus the new datum center. Need investigate whether that bound transfers to the explicit leave-one-out partition initialization of Algorithm 2; the old remaining-cluster center changes when seed is removed. No counterexample has yet been established. Do not claim a disproven bound based only on this concern.

passages.locator: PDF pp. 5-6 / pp. 1185-1186, Section IV-B, Equations 5-11
passages.reading: CMM acceleration fits once a positive-support simplex q using S_ij=exp(-beta*(K_ii+K_jj-2K_ij)), q_new_j=q_j*(1/N)*sum_i S_ij/(sum_l S_il q_l). Select P highest q after their indices and ordering stabilize for an unspecified number of iterations; P supplied, usually M<P<<N. This is not objective convergence. Then try only those candidate seeds at each stage and retain best partition. All N observations still participate in clustering. Beta guide N^2 logN/sum_ij dist². Gaussian and atomic-density interpretations need the same qualifications as earlier CMM records; finite positive-affinity optimization is well-defined without an asserted RKHS density. This complete initialization strategy differs from the CMM hard clustering policy.

passages.locator: PDF pp. 6-7 / pp. 1186-1187, Section V, Equations 12-19
passages.reading: Positive observation weights a_i give weighted feature means and E=sum_i a_i distance². Weighted global uses same seed stages and weighted local fit. Weighted fast uses b_n=sum_i a_i max(d_i_old-dist²(i,n),0). Weighted CMM uses empirical p_i=a_i/sum a: q_new_j=q_j sum_i p_i S_ij/z_i. Its beta guide is N*H(p)/sum_ij p_i dist²(i,j). Observation weights differ from learned view weights. Scaling all a uniformly leaves fits and p unchanged, rescales E and b. Formula conditions include positive cluster weight and nonzero beta-guide denominator.

passages.locator: PDF pp. 7-8 / pp. 1187-1188, Section VI, Equations 20-21
passages.reading: For symmetric graph A, ratio association uses a_i=1,K=A; normalized cut uses positive degree weights a_i=D_ii and K=D^-1 A D^-1. PSD sufficient for kernel descent. Diagonal shift lambda I for RA or lambda D^-1 for NC makes K PSD if large enough, preserving fixed-M objective ordering through a constant offset, but can change iteration paths and local minima. Degree-zero nodes need convention. Experiments use only a small diagonal shift, explicitly not necessarily ensuring PSD; empirical convergence does not establish the PSD guarantee.

passages.locator: PDF pp. 8-13 / pp. 1188-1193, Section VII, Tables II-VI and Figures 1-4
passages.reading: Read all synthetic ring, digit, Olivetti and graph comparisons. Fixed Gaussian sigma empirically selected; M supplied, often known class count. Its graph-based relaxation motivates the method, while the efficient out-of-sample algorithm uses a fitted rectangular distribution instead of eigendecomposing the complete empirical graph for every query. Equation (2) prints Y^T Y=I while retaining unscaled plus/minus-one entries. Equation (1) instead implies Y^T Y=nI for n observations; an identity normalization requires rescaled real-valued relaxed coordinates. The record preserves this distinction rather than copying the incompatible constraints.

Equation (4) gives the interval width but omits the origin shift unless its x already denotes a shifted coordinate. The mechanism states that shift explicitly. Degenerate axes, zero-threshold ties and points outside fitted intervals require explicit numerical conventions.

Continuous orthogonality does not guarantee empirical balance, decorrelation or independence after thresholding. Excluding outer-product modes avoids one explicit source of deterministic redundancy but does not ensure independent bits; even first and third thresholded modes on one uniform axis are correlated.

The number of bits need not be smaller than the input dimension. Compact storage and approximate-neighbor retrieval are not a guarantee of dimension reduction, exact semantic similarity, universal retrieval accuracy or collision resistance for cryptography. claims.statement: The motivation minimizes affinity-weighted squared distances between binary codes, subject to balanced bits and pairwise decorrelation; dropping the binary restriction yields low nonconstant graph-Laplacian modes. The practical algorithm first computes PCA coordinates and fits an interval [a_j,b_j] along each retained nondegenerate axis. Under its uniform-rectangle approximation, enumerate nonconstant single-axis modes with positive integer frequency m, represented in shifted coordinates by cos(m*pi*(x_j-a_j)/(b_j-a_j)). Rank these modes by their analytic eigenvalue order, equivalently increasing squared frequency (m/(b_j-a_j))^2 for a common positive bandwidth, and select the required number of bits. Exclude the constant mode and multidimensional outer-product modes. Threshold each selected function at zero to form binary codes. A new point is projected into the same PCA coordinates and evaluated by these selected functions; hash-table retrieval then compares codes within a chosen Hamming radius.

claims.statement: Given N aligned observations, V fixed positive-semidefinite view Gram matrices K_v, a supplied cluster count M and exponent p>=1, form Ktilde=sum_v w_v^p K_v with nonnegative w and sum_v w_v=1. The actual kernel coefficients are w_v^p, which need not sum to one. Their feature map concatenates the view features scaled by sqrt(w_v^p). The supplied kernels, M and p are not all learned by this procedure.

evidence.locator: Section IV-A, PDF p. 3, Equations 4-7

claims.statement: For fixed w, choose N-by-M Y with Y^T Y=I spanning a leading M-dimensional eigenspace of the raw composite kernel Ktilde. This minimizes tr(Ktilde)-tr(Y^T Ktilde Y) over that relaxed set. Then compute D_v=tr(K_v)-tr(Y^T K_v Y) and update w by the conditional weight solution. Repeat without discretizing Y between weight updates. The paper starts w uniformly and applies k-means-based discretization to the final eigenvector embedding after convergence. That postprocessing is separate from the relaxed optimization and may lose its optimal value.

evidence.locator: Section III-B, PDF p. 3, Equation 3; Section IV-B.2/4/5, PDF p. 4; Section IV-C, PDF p. 5; Appendix B, PDF p. 10

claims.statement: For fixed positive residuals D_v and p>1, minimize sum_v D_v*w_v^p on the simplex using w_v=D_v^(-1/(p-1))/sum_u D_u^(-1/(p-1)). This gives positive weights for every positive residual. If some residuals are zero, the ratio formula is undefined; any weights supported entirely on zero-residual views minimize the block. At p=1, select a minimum-residual view as in the source, while ties mathematically permit any simplex distribution over minimizers. Neither zero-residual nor tied cases imply a unique weight vector.

evidence.locator: Section IV-B, PDF p. 4, Equations 9-10; Appendices A-B, PDF p. 10, Equations 11-18; curator zero-residual and tied-minimum checks

claims.statement: For fixed positive residuals, increasing p makes the simplex weight ratio (D_u/D_v)^(1/(p-1)) approach one. The ratio of actual kernel coefficients is (D_u/D_v)^(p/(p-1)); as p grows it approaches D_u/D_v, not generally one. Thus nearly uniform w does not imply uniform effective kernel contributions. The source uses sparsity to describe relative concentration; finite p>1 with positive residuals does not select exact zeros. The power-of-simplex constraint is not an asserted equivalence to every conventional lp multiple-kernel regularizer.

evidence.locator: Section IV-C, PDF pp. 4-5; Equation 4 and related norm discussion, PDF p. 3; curator large-p calculation

claims.statement: View residual scales affect the learned weights. The source divides each view kernel by its mean pairwise squared feature distance, N^(-2)*sum_ij(K_vii-2*K_vij+K_vjj), to make scales comparable. This denominator vanishes for a constant feature view and needs an explicit convention. Such normalization does not establish that weights quantify semantic reliability or that a method is immune to uninformative views.

evidence.locator: Section IV-C, PDF p. 5, last paragraph; Section V-B, PDF pp. 6-7; curator constant-kernel and rescaling checks

claims.statement: Exact spectral and weight block updates do not increase the nonnegative relaxed objective, so its values converge. This alone does not prove unique parameter convergence or that every coordinatewise fixed point is a joint local minimum. For K_1=diag(1,0), K_2=diag(0,1), M=1 and p=2, w=(1/2,1/2) gives a tied composite eigenspace. Choosing Y=(1,1)/sqrt(2) is a valid fixed spectral/weight update with objective 1/4, yet an arbitrarily small joint rotation and weight adjustment lowers the objective. This curator example qualifies the source local-minimum claim under allowed eigenvalue ties; it does not reproduce the source experiments.

# Curator derivation: singleton removal preserves the fast error bound

The 2009 paper's Algorithm 2 removes seed n from its old cluster before using it as a new singleton. This changes that old cluster's mean. The bound in IV-A nevertheless extends to this initialization when cluster weights remain positive and the local updates are well-defined.

Use an RKHS, observation weights a_i>0, and an old cluster C of weight W with mean mu. The seed has weight a<W and centered vector z=phi(x_n)-mu. Removing it shifts the mean by delta=-a*z/(W-a). Compare with the hypothetical nearest-center assignment that retains all old means and adds phi(x_n). Its error is E_old-b_n (assuming old assigned distances are nearest-center distances, as after converged local fitting).

Within C, let R be those assigned to the new seed in that hypothetical comparison, choosing the seed itself to join R in a tie. Write B=sum_{i in R} a_i, so B>=a. Each i in R obeys 2*<phi(x_i)-mu,z> >= ||z||^2. The old weighted centered vectors sum to zero. For S=C\R, the change in cost from evaluating their distances at mu+delta rather than mu is

Delta = -2*a/(W-a) * sum_{i in R} a_i*<phi(x_i)-mu,z>
        + (W-B)*a^2/(W-a)^2 * ||z||^2
      <= a*W*(a-B)/(W-a)^2 * ||z||^2 <= 0.

All other old clusters retain their means, and R retains the seed center. Thus this comparison assignment costs at most E_old-b_n with the actual initialized centers. The actual nearest-center reassignment can only lower this cost, as can weighted-mean recomputation and further exact Lloyd steps. The argument also covers z=0. It does not resolve empty-cluster policies, non-PSD similarities, arbitrary approximate updates, or arbitrary empty-cluster repair. If an old source cluster is a singleton (a=W), the displayed initialization itself needs a convention.

This is a curator derivation of a source-supported claim, not source text or a historical code reproduction. A separate seeded unweighted two-dimensional probe found no counterexample in 10,000 datasets under defined nonempty runs; that finite probe alone is not a proof.
